nodes.name: Impregnation and Calcination of CoOx Catalysts
nodes.procedure: The Co(NO3)2 precursor was impregnated onto commercial SiO2 and CeO2 oxides, followed by calcination at 400 °C (5 h in air) to form CoOx/SiO2 and CoOx/CeO2 catalysts.

unit_operations.name: Calcination

nodes.name: Impregnation and Calcination of Pt Catalysts
nodes.procedure: The Pt(NO3)2 precursor was impregnated onto the same SiO2 and CeO2 materials used above and then calcined at 400 °C in air for 5 h to form Pt/CeO2 and Pt/SiO2 catalysts.

nodes.name: Preparation of Pt on Various Supports
nodes.procedure: Pt(NO3)2 precursor was impregnated onto various oxide supports (gamma-Al2O3, Nb2O5, ZrO2, TiO2, and Ce0.6Zr0.4O2) followed by calcination at 400 °C in air for 5 h.
nodes.source_text: Pt and CoOx catalysts are also deposited onto various oxide supports (i.e., γ-Al2O3, Nb2O5, ZrO2, TiO2, and solid solution Ce0.6Zr0.4O2)... Pt species are highly dispersed on these oxide supports... [methods similar to 0.7 wt% Pt/CeO2]

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows pure support structures (CeO2 and SiO2) without crystalline Co oxide phases, indicating high dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD patterns from the as-prepared catalysts exhibit pure CeO2 ... and SiO2 ... structures but without any crystalline phases of Co oxide

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectroscopy shows A1g peak shifts; Co-O bond force constants (k) were calculated as 348 N/m for CoOx/CeO2 and 358 N/m for CoOx/SiO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: k is 345, 348, and 358 N/m for Co3O4, CoOx/CeO2, and CoOx/SiO2 catalysts (Figure 1e)

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS reveals surface Co species on SiO2 are 79% Co2+ and 21% Co3+, while CeO2 support has 45% Co3+.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS results displayed in Figure 2a indicate that the surface Co species of CoOx/SiO2 catalyst are mainly Co2+ (79%) and only contain a small amount of Co3+ (21%).

nodes.characterization_summary: H2-TPR shows reduction peaks at 275 and 358 °C for CoOx/CeO2, while reduction to Co0 for CoOx/SiO2 is shifted to a higher temperature of 690 °C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For CoOx/SiO2, the temperature at which Co2+ is reduced to metallic Co shifts to 690 °C ... peaks at 275 and 358 °C for CoOx/CeO2

nodes.characterization_summary: After aging at 800 °C in air, metallic Pt peaks (39.7° and 46.2°) appear for Pt/SiO2 but not for Pt/CeO2, indicating sintering on SiO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: sharp diffraction peaks attributed to large Pt nanoparticles are present in the XRD patterns of Pt/SiO2-S but not for Pt/CeO2-S
